Q: Elegant way to do Chained Null Checks A:

Check my answer here

https://stackoverflow.com/a/34086283/4711853

you could simply write small extension method, which afford you to write chained lambda like this:

var val = instance.DefaultOrValue(x => x.SecondInstance) .DefaultOrValue(x => x.ThirdInstance) .DefaultOrValue(x => x.Value);

you may name this method shortier

Q: MySQL I dont want my SUM CASE to be Null A:

The problem is that game_id can have an empty game_score field in one row and a valid one in another. Your code picks up the valid one and returns non-null.

Fix this problem by looking for this case explicitly, as the first argument to coalesce:

SELECT game_id, (CASE WHEN count(*) <> count(game_score) then NULL ELSE COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN game_score = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), . . .

I'm not sure what the coalesce is trying to do. It seems to be adding one for a bunch of different game_scores. Can you use one of the following instead:

COUNT(game_score) ?

SUM(case when game_score between 1 and xx then 1 else 0 end) ?

Q: Wrong language shown in AppStore A:

I had an app published on the AppStore for monthes with EN as main language instead of FR. When I decided to tackle this issue and try to have the right language displayed on the AppStore, I tried many of the advices found on Google. After half a dozen changes and re-publications on Apple Store Connect, I finally made it.

I am still unsure which of the changes I brought were decisive but here are some advices:

  1. to avoid having to distribute the app, wait for approval by Apple and then check on the AppStore if the language is correctly changed, just archive your project and check inside the build:

    1. in Xcode, you can access your archive by Window > Organizer

    2. right-click on the latest archive and select Show in Finder...

    3. open your archive with right-click Display content of Package

    4. open the folder: Products/Applications to find your archive

    5. right-click on YourApp and again Display Content of Package

    6. Here if you find a file en.lproj then for sure the main language of your app will be EN

  2. the change that finally got me rid of the en.lproj file that was to create a Localizable.xcstring file in the root of the project (I had one but in the target instead)

Other things I did before that :

  1. force developpement region in your project.pbxproj

    1. Right Click on *.xcodeproj

    2. Show package contents

    3. Open project.pbxproj

    4. Find : developmentRegion = en;

    5. Replace with : developmentRegion = fr; (or whatever your target language is)

    6. Save

    7. I am not sure, but instead of steps 1. through 6. it might be equivalent (and probably better practice) to go to: Product > Scheme > Edit Scheme and there, update both App Language and App Region to what you target.

  2. force Base SDK -> iOS

    1. in : TARGET/Build Settings set Base SDK to iOS

    2. if Automatic is selected the title of the Info properties list might be Custom MacOS Target Properties instead of Custom iOS Target Properties and the correct language might not be taken in account.

Q: How to add multiple .env files into nuxt? A:

According to this issue, it's not currently possible (in Nuxt v4) to pass in multiple --dotenv parameters. See: https://github.com/nuxt/cli/issues/1248

As a workaround you can use dotenv-cli:

dotenv -e .env.development -e .env -- nuxt dev

Note that dotenv resolves env vars by "first-wins" so ABC in .env.development will override any ABC in .env.

Q: Is there such a thing as short-circuit evaluation within a regular expression? If so, how to write it? A:

Is there a way to write the regular expression such that it captures nothing and stops searching at the first match?

That's what it does by default. You have to use the -all switch to make it search for all the matches and return the number found. Without this, it simply returns 1 as soon as it finds a match.

Regarding some of the other issues you raised, you can use (?:...) to create a non-capturing group. You can also use [[,] to match a square bracket or comma, rather than alternation \[|, in a group. Or use [[:<:]] and [[:>:]] to match the beginning and end of a word, respectively, rather than matching the punctuation characters explicitly. So the regexp could be

[[:<:]](?:$rnodes)[[:>:]]
